current_first_party_scope.guard_use: rime_jni.cc notificationHandler lambda, auto env at line 251

lifetime_proof: The notification lambda declares its JEnv guard before its JRef array. Reverse scope destruction deletes the array before detaching the owned environment.
The JString temporary passed to SetObjectArrayElement is destroyed at the end of that full expression, before CallStaticVoidMethod begins.
CallStaticVoidMethod returns before the callback scope ends. The lambda returns void; it does not return a JNI local reference or JNIEnv pointer after the owner dies.
All object conversion factories take the caller-provided JNIEnv directly; none creates its own short-lived JEnv guard around a returned jobject.
Reentrant Java-to-native notifications see GetEnv=JNI_OK, borrow the existing environment, and do not detach it while the outer Java call is active.
Kotlin creates message objects and stores ordinary Java references in handlers/flow. Those Java references are not the native local-reference handles being deleted or invalidated by detach.
The JNI globals are NewGlobalRef references initialized by GlobalRefSingleton and remain valid across a thread detach; this patch does not change that constructor.

Pinned librime Deployer::StartWork uses std::async in threaded mode, and Run emits deploy messages. The source contains a native-worker route to this callback, so attachment cleanup is not merely an abstract helper use.

mock_regression.scope: Unmodified existing seven-case JNI function-table mock, including attach/GetEnv failures and copy/move traits. The runner changed only baseline/header-head preconditions and output location.

remaining_limits: GetEnv or AttachCurrentThread failure can still leave env null; current callback dereference lacks a guard. This existed before the patch and is not claimed fixed.
DetachCurrentThread return status remains ignored. This review establishes the normal current callback has completed its Java call before owning guard destruction, not every possible external misuse.

The callback does not check or propagate a Java exception from CallStaticVoidMethod. Detaching with a pending exception may cause the VM to report it; failure-injection callback semantics were not changed or tested here.

JEnv is lexically thread-confined. Destroying it via an external pointer on a different thread, manually detaching/re-attaching inside its scope, or retaining a local JNI handle beyond the owner remains invalid usage; no such current callsite was found.

The implicit raw-JNIEnv conversion could allow future misuse such as assigning a temporary AttachEnv result to a raw pointer. The current callsite uses auto and keeps the owner alive. This is a future API-footgun boundary, not an observed current callsite bug.
Owned native callbacks will attach/detach per callback; actual Android notification throughput and Java-thread identity/performance effects were not measured.
Real HotSpot plus checked-JNI verifies JNI attachment behavior on a host JVM, not ART, Android, a complete Rime callback, OEM behavior, Release or runtime acceptance.
Only the original split head had the prior four-OS application CI. New submission-head CI must be reported separately; these host checks do not stand in for it.
recommendation: Suitable as one focused Draft PR with explicit tested scope and pending ART acceptance; no blocking lifetime/cross-thread-detach error was found in the current first-party callsites.

reproducer.usage: python3 reproduce-host-vm.py --repo REPO --base BASE --head HEAD --ndk NDK --jdk JDK --out OUT
reproducer.expected: The leaking baseline exits 1 after explicit test cleanup; fixed exits 0. Both DestroyJavaVM calls must finish. The checked-JNI rerun repeats the same cases, adding no case count.
